a: Nixarchy is AI-first: pick your coding agent once and everything AI (this helper's chat, crash diagnosis, SUPER+A) uses it. Open the menu with SUPER+SPACE, go to Setup → Default agent, and choose (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini…). Or in a terminal: omarchy default agent claude. Then sign in to the agent once and you're set.

SUPER (the Windows key) runs everything. SUPER+SPACE opens the Omarchy menu — apps, install, style, setup, power. SUPER+K shows every keybinding on your machine, including your own custom ones. When lost, press SUPER+K.
SUPER+RETURN opens a terminal. SUPER+SHIFT+RETURN opens the browser (and SUPER+ALT+RETURN opens tmux). Or press SUPER+SPACE and type any app's name, like a search bar.

SUPER+C copies, SUPER+V pastes, SUPER+X cuts — the same keys in every app, including the terminal (no more Ctrl+Shift+C gymnastics). SUPER+CTRL+V opens your clipboard history so you can paste something from earlier.

SUPER+W closes the focused window (many apps here have no titlebar buttons — this is the way). Hold SUPER and drag with the left mouse button to move a floating window; SUPER + right-button drag resizes it.

This is the one thing NixOS really does differently. Open the package manager: SUPER+SPACE → Install → Packages (or SUPER+ALT+N, if that key is bound on your machine). Search, tick what you want, and apply with one key. Ticking does NOT install anything: it writes your choice into ~/.config/nixarchy/apps.nix, and nothing changes until you apply. Applying rebuilds the system and makes every queued choice real at once. From a terminal it is the same: nixarchy search to browse everything, or nixarchy pkg add <name>, then nixarchy apply. If you don't see Packages, the panel may be off: Setup → Plugins.

q: Why did my install not happen?
a: Because nothing on NixOS is installed until you rebuild. The Install menu queues your choice in ~/.config/nixarchy/apps.nix; nixarchy apply is what applies it. That is the trade: you can see your whole machine in one file, copy it to another laptop, and undo any change. Note that installing with pacman, yay or a downloaded binary will not work here — the package has to go in the file.

SUPER+SPACE → Remove → Package deselects it, or from a terminal: nixarchy app disable <id> (nixarchy app remove picks interactively). As with installing, it only edits the file — run nixarchy apply to make it real. Nothing is left behind afterwards: the old packages are garbage-collected, not orphaned.

q: Turn a website into an app
a: SUPER+SPACE → Install → Web App. Give it a name, the URL, and an icon — it wraps the site as a real app with its own window and launcher entry. Great for Gmail, WhatsApp Web, YouTube, dashboards. This is how several of the preinstalled 'apps' work, and it needs no rebuild.

q: A toolchain just for one project
a: Don't install compilers system-wide — give each project its own. Open SUPER+SPACE → Apps → Dev environments (SUPER+ALT+E where it is bound) to create a project from a template, enter it, or see every project that has one. In a terminal, the same thing is nixarchy dev init <preset> in the project folder (run it with no argument to list presets: node, python, go, rust…). It writes a devenv.nix, and from then on the toolchain appears when you cd into that folder and disappears when you leave. Two projects can use two different versions of the same language without clashing. No Dev environments entry? It comes with the devenv service: nixarchy-service-enable devenv, then nixarchy apply.

Open the Podman panel: SUPER+SPACE → Apps → Podman (SUPER+ALT+O where it is bound). It lists containers, images, volumes and networks, and starts, stops, follows logs and opens a shell without you remembering flags. In a terminal it is plain podman, rootless. The docker command keeps meaning Docker, which is still nixarchy's default engine. No Podman entry? It comes with the podman service: nixarchy-service-enable podman, then nixarchy apply. If it is installed but off, turn it on in Setup → Plugins.

q: Software that only ships for Ubuntu or Arch
a: Some programs only come as a .deb, or only in the AUR, and will not run on NixOS as they are. Put them in a box: a whole other Linux distribution running inside nixarchy, sharing your home folder and your screen. Open SUPER+SPACE → Trigger → Boxes (SUPER+ALT+D where it is bound), create a box from a template, enter it, and install the program with that distribution's own tools. In a terminal it is distrobox. No Boxes entry? Turn boxes on: nixarchy-service-enable boxes, then nixarchy apply.

Independent desks for separate contexts — browser on one, work on another. SUPER+1…9 jumps to a workspace (they're created as you visit them). SUPER+SHIFT+1…9 sends the focused window to that workspace. The numbers in your top bar show which desk you're on.

SUPER+arrow keys move focus between windows in the direction you press. SUPER+SHIFT+arrows swap the windows themselves. New windows tile automatically — nothing overlaps unless it's a floating window.

A hidden overlay workspace: press SUPER+S and it drops over whatever you're doing; press SUPER+S again and it's gone — but everything in it keeps running. Send any window there with SUPER+ALT+S. Perfect for a terminal, music player, or chat you want one keypress away.

q: Make a window fill the screen
a: SUPER+F expands the focused window within the layout; SUPER+CTRL+F is true fullscreen (bar hidden). Press the same key again to go back. Exact behavior can vary if customized — SUPER+K shows what yours does.

SUPER+SPACE → Style → Theme. One choice restyles everything at once — colors, bar, terminal, lock screen, wallpaper. Many themes ship with the system and you can install more from git URLs (Style → Theme → Install). Backgrounds cycle with SUPER+CTRL+SPACE. Themes are the same as on Omarchy and need no rebuild.

Brightness usually lives on your keyboard's function keys. Display settings (resolution, scaling, arrangement) are in SUPER+SPACE → Setup → Monitors — it edits ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua for you, which is yours to keep and survives every rebuild. Night-light and idle/lock timing are under Setup too.
SUPER+SPACE → Setup → Wi-Fi opens the network picker; Setup → Bluetooth pairs devices. Both also sit as icons in the top bar — click them for the same panels. Neither needs a rebuild.

Press PRINT — select an area, and it opens in a small editor for arrows/text before saving to your Pictures folder (and the clipboard). SUPER+CTRL+PRINT grabs TEXT from anywhere on screen via OCR — great for copying from images or videos.

SUPER+SPACE → Update, or run: omarchy update (nixarchy update is the same command). On NixOS this updates your flake inputs and rebuilds the whole system as one atomic step — it either fully succeeds or changes nothing. The desktop session you're sitting in isn't disturbed; a new kernel or driver only takes effect after a reboot.

You can always go back — this is NixOS's best feature. Every rebuild keeps the previous system as a 'generation', and the boot menu lists them: reboot and pick the one before the problem. To step back without rebooting: sudo nixos-rebuild switch --rollback. Nothing is lost, because the old system was never deleted in the first place.

q: Try something in a throwaway VM
a: Want to try a risky tool or a config change without touching this machine? Start a MicroVM: SUPER+SPACE → Trigger → Sandbox (SUPER+ALT+V where it is bound). Pick a template, and a small NixOS machine boots in seconds, sharing your /nix/store read-only. It is a console, not a desktop. Throw it away when you are done and nothing is left behind. It keeps an untrusted package off your machine; it is not a wall against an attacker. In a terminal it is nixarchy vm (nixarchy vm help lists what it can do).
SUPER+SPACE → Power has lock, suspend, restart, and shutdown. The screen locks automatically after idle (timing under Setup → Idle). Closing the laptop lid suspends by default.

If a program crashes, you get a notification offering an AI diagnosis — click it and your default agent investigates the crash for you. Nothing set up? It only appears once you've chosen your default agent (see 'Set up your AI agent').
